findings.claim: time.active_s and throughput_per_h treat every gap over sleep_gap_ms between consecutive ledger lines as quiet time. During a step no script writes a ledger line (no heartbeat kind in CONTRACT 3.7; the watcher writes only event lines), so the session's working hours are subtracted as 'quiet'. throughput_per_h then comes out far too high, or null.
findings.evidence: By hand: a bind line at 10:00, intake at 11:00:00, commit at 11:00:05, 3 ids covered, sleep_gap 600000. Quiet is 3600 s, wall_s 3605, active_s 5, so throughput = 3/(5/3600) = 2160 per hour. With only bind and commit 2 h apart, active_s is 0 and throughput is null. T15 passes only because its fixture puts ledger lines less than 10 min apart.
findings.fix: Divide throughput by wall_s hours and keep quiet_gaps and active_s as readings. Better: take activity gaps from the model-call timestamps of the task's own transcripts (parsed already in loadSession), not from ledger lines.

findings.claim: plants pooling sums k, found and contra_found over every stored x_ certificate, so a re-certified review counts two or three times. contra_k counts the against-hope plants of every sealed/plants file, including tasks that have no certificate yet. The numerator and denominator cover different sets, and the Clopper-Pearson bounds are too narrow.
findings.evidence: Two certificates for one review, each {k:3, found:3}, pool to 6/6 instead of 3/3. Plants for tasks A and B, each with one against-hope plant, and only A certified with contra_found 1, give contra_rate 1/2 instead of 1/1.
findings.fix: Pool one certificate per task: the latest, or the VALID one per tms labels. Take contra_k only from the sealed/plants files of the tasks in that set.

findings.claim: In freeze and post-review batches every seed item carries the same synthetic sentence: sid 's1', fixed template text, and applies_to equal to the card's full conditions. Real items carry authored sentences, so a checker can pick out up to 7 seeds by their sentences. This breaks R42/R43: the checker must not be able to tell a seed from a real item.
findings.evidence: syntheticSentence() returns a constant shape. withSentence is true in every non-intake mode. T6 checks key sets only, not text shape.
findings.fix: Build each seed's sentence from a real fact sentence of the same committed object, changing only what the operator needs. Or vary the phrasing with rng and use unused sids. Add a test that no sentence text is shared by all seed items.

findings.claim: The coordinator form never checks helper reads: udi_reads is main-only and no read_prefixes are applied to helpers. The checker is a coordinator helper, so reading sealed/seeds/<b>.json (the key) or a second batch is never flagged. CONTRACT 3.21 says audit flags a checker that reads more than one batch. The task form's {batch} expansion also allows every batch.
findings.evidence: readsOf(main) only at line 458. There is no helper read loop in coordinatorForm. {batch} is expanded to all batchDirs at line 235 with no count of distinct batches.
findings.fix: For each checker helper transcript, apply tcb/profiles/checker.json read_prefixes with {batch} bound to the batch it read first. List any other read in checker_reads and exit 1 when that list is not empty.

findings.claim: isExcludedCard treats only rejected and superseded cards as untrusted. Pending and unverifiable cards are not trusted under R24 ('witnessed or confirmed'), yet they render in the main pack body. They also feed synthesis effects and can set 'weak: disagreement'.
findings.evidence: A confirmed card with effect improves plus a pending card with effect worsens on one key gives weak: true from an unchecked card.

findings.claim: With f5_given true, isCounted ignores the 'superseded' label (R16 overrides every status). A replaced card still counts for coverage, held-out recall, Chapman and throughput. The f5-false branch does exclude it.
findings.evidence: Card A confirmed, superseded by B confirmed: both count, raising recall and inflating Chapman n1/n2/m.
findings.fix: Add && cardLabel(id) !== 'superseded' to the f5 branch.

findings.claim: Removing the shuffle (const order = all) passes every test. Seeds then always sit after the real items, which breaks R42's 'random position'.
findings.evidence: Mutation C3 left 22 pass, 0 fail. T5 compares item-id arrays, which differ anyway because the seed contents change with the rng.
findings.fix: Assert that the seed positions in batch.json change with the rng seed and are not always after every real item.

findings.claim: Removing the epoch re-check inside the lock passes every test. A fence that lands between the pre-lock check and the lock would let a stale attempt's audit be written.
findings.evidence: Mutation A1 left 20 pass. T15 exercises only the pre-lock compare at line 180.
findings.fix: Test with a lock held by a test-spawned holder while the row's epoch is raised. Expect 65 and no file.

findings.claim: Removing the --ce check inside the run lock passes all render and audit tests. CONTRACT 1.1 requires it inside the lock.
findings.evidence: Mutations R9 (26 pass) and A12 (20 pass).
findings.fix: Change coord.json ce while a test-held lock blocks the script, then release it. Expect 64 and no write.

findings.claim: Weakening the R30 rule from 'last non-blank line is TURN-END <field>' to 'any line is' passes every test, so a note after TURN-END is never exercised.
findings.fix: Add the turn end 'TURN-END f1\nextra note' to T10 as a bad case.

findings.claim: Removing the commit-record sha256 comparison passes every test. T7 edits object bytes, which getObject's 16-hex name check catches anyway, so an edited record sha256 is never tested.
findings.fix: In T7, also edit an output's sha256 in the commit record and expect exit 3 object-mismatch.

findings.claim: Removing S1's 'redrawn until not in window' check passes every test: the redraw branch is never run.
findings.fix: In T2, pass an rng stub whose first draw yields a quote placed in the window, and assert that the result differs from it.

verdict: The four scripts follow their specs closely, and all 106 tests run clean (93 pass, 13 needs-app skips). Of 40 mutations, 31 were caught. One high finding: render's throughput per active hour drops every ledger silence over 10 min, and a working session writes no ledger lines, so its working time is dropped. Medium findings: seed's plant pool double-counts re-certified reviews and takes its contra denominator from a different set. Render trusts pending and unverifiable cards (against R24) and, with f5_given, still counts superseded cards for coverage. Seed sentences are a fixed template that tells them apart from real ones. The coordinator audit never sees what the checker helper reads. Test gaps where a mutation survived: the in-lock epoch and ce checks, the seed shuffle, the TURN-END last-line rule, the commit-record sha and the S1 window check.
